executiveSummary: GM0085 Ooststellingwerf was the first lexicographically pending municipality with an absent artifact after excluding the two assigned codes. The official/generated 2025 identity, 25,925 residents, 59 neighbourhoods in thirteen districts, thirteen BAG woonplaatsen, 34 settlement labels and nine logical road-border records are coherent. Neighbourhood rows total 25,940 residents, fifteen above the municipality control (+0.058%); the allocator reconciles this independent CBS rounding without overwriting published values. All ten presets run deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across eight services, with bounded values, service-layer-invariant hazard, exact no-event behavior, causal-ledger closure and monotone event-attributable burden. Release is nevertheless correction-required. The major-river preset publishes 0.513332 m at T+24 and T+72 although Ooststellingwerf is governed by the Boven Tjonger, Grootdiep, Kleindiep, Opsterlandse Compagnonsvaart, De Linde and cross-border Drenthe water systems rather than a Rhine/Meuse/IJssel inundation source. Pluvial publishes 0.347866 m without the water board's named wetness, drainage, groundwater, storage and receiving-level mechanisms. Eight materially different nonzero T+24 hazards reuse exactly the same full neighbourhood order. The canonical wildfire produces zero direct local fire and remote smoke; a controlled ignition at Appelscha-Buitengebied leaves that source neighbourhood only 24th of 59, despite the official Drents-Friese Wold/Fochteloërveen nature-fire pathway. The fixed earthquake gives 0.083880 g at T+6 without a selected KNMI event, shakemap or vulnerability surface. The municipality has no ProRail station and no RIVM SEH point, while 69 scheduled bus stops and nine N381/N353/N917/N919/N979/N351/N380 border records are static context, not incident throughput or external acute-care access. The partial HWH snapshot contains 204 weirs, fifteen surface-water pumps, six sluices, nine sewer pumps and two wastewater plants; rwzi Haulerwijk is explicitly marked buiten bedrijf and must not be treated as available. One Liander planning sample, future grid projects, 73 antennas and 21 education locations do not establish topology, live state, backup or restoration. Safety-region evidence also identifies technological risks from facilities, transport and pipelines involving flammable, explosive or toxic substances, a missing local scenario family. No reviewed public source confirms incident-ready support points, capacity, stocks or auditable T+0–72 actions. Unknown water, road, bus, care, utility, industrial, visitor and response state remains Unknown or NoData, never safe or zero.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0085 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, woonplaats and settlement inputs
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated CBS/BAG/BRT snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; audited 3 September 2026
supports: The annual official/generated row identifies GM0085 as Ooststellingwerf and reports 25,925 residents, density 116/km², 26.5% aged 65-plus and 4,022 one-person households. CBS/PDOK is CC BY 4.0 and is static demographic context, not incident occupancy or individual vulnerability.

The municipality reference point [6.257309770000922,52.98900329551465] lies inside the generalized 2025 boundary. The outline is fit for administrative aggregation, not water, sewer, road, utility, nature-fire or building connectivity.

Fifty-nine neighbourhood rows in thirteen districts sum to 25,940 residents (+15, +0.058%), 11,650 households and 6,850 independently rounded residents aged 65-plus. Model reconciliation preserves the source rows.
BAG supplies thirteen woonplaatsen and BRT supplies 34 locality labels. BAG/PDOK is Public Domain Mark 1.0 and BRT is CC BY 4.0; place, label and demographic provenance remains distinct.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Watergebiedsplan Appelscha local surface-water, groundwater and drainage mechanisms
evidenceSources.edition: Published water-area plan for Appelscha and surroundings; current public document inspected 3 September 2026; no standard reuse licence found
supports: The plan identifies water nuisance around Weperpolder, Haule, Rolpaal and west Oosterwolde, and at the Opsterlandse Compagnonsvaart/Boven Tjonger crossing when heavy rain combines with high Tjongerkanaal levels. It also identifies Grootdiep/Boven Tjonger constraints.

Fochteloo has wetness from low terrain, keileem, poor runoff and seepage; north Langedijke/Kleindiep has rapid level rise from narrow channels and little storage; south Oosterwolde and east Appelscha have poor drainage; east Makkinga has narrow-channel inundation risk.

The plan records peak-rain inflow from Drenthe across the provincial boundary, while Haulerpolder and Appelschaaster Maden also have drought/low-groundwater mechanisms. These are spatially differentiated official planning mechanisms, not current observations or forecasts.
The public plan does not by itself provide live structure state, a selected rainfall field, an event hydrograph, metre-depth raster, arrival/recession clock or operational capacity.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Regional risk analysis and official Ooststellingwerf municipal risk profile
evidenceSources.edition: Regional risk-profile municipal images and risk analysis 2022; current public copies inspected 3 September 2026; no standard reuse licence found
supports: The Ooststellingwerf profile identifies nature areas, vulnerable objects for reduced self-reliance, large public functions, provincial roads and possible failure of all vital-infrastructure types.

It identifies technological risks from facilities, transport and pipelines involving flammable, explosive or toxic substances. These mechanisms are omitted by the canonical ten presets and cannot be represented as generic cyber or fire effects.

The regional analysis records a GRIP-2 fire in Fochteloërveen on 25 April 2011 and multiple large nature fires in southeast Fryslân. Its Drents-Friese Wold scenario includes fire spread toward inhabited areas, two care homes and a large recreation park, road closure, summer visitors and difficult access over unpaved sand paths.
Historic incidents and official scenarios establish plausible mechanisms and planning needs, not current ignition, probability, casualties, occupancy or guaranteed resources.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Drents-Friese Wold wildfire, drought, climate and first-response context
evidenceSources.edition: Staatsbosbeheer nature-fire publication May 2025; municipal heat and climate-adaptation pages published June–August 2026; inspected 3 September 2026; no standard reuse licence found
supports: Staatsbosbeheer describes the Drents-Friese Wold as a large continuous nature area with real wildfire risk under longer dry periods and documents joint route sharing, training and exercises by Drenthe and Fryslân fire services. The park is about 6,100 hectares across the provincial boundary, with about 4,000 hectares managed by Staatsbosbeheer.

The municipality's dated 2026 heat communication links persistent drought to elevated nature-fire likelihood and asks residents to check neighbours. This is dated public guidance, not a current incident observation or a measured outreach action.
The municipality announced a climate-adaptation subsidy for water nuisance, heat and drought starting October 2026. A future measure must not be modeled as already completed protection.

No reviewed public source confirms an incident-ready support point, capacity, generator, potable-water stock, staffing, accessibility or activation state. The Appelscha visitor centre, schools and care locations are ordinary facilities unless an authority assigns an emergency role.

evidenceSources.publisher: Gemeente Ooststellingwerf / Provincie Fryslân / Rijkswaterstaat / OVapi / ProRail
evidenceSources.title: E05 — N381 and other road corridors, scheduled bus, no-station and industrial context
evidenceSources.edition: Municipal current business-area page; NWB-Light 1 August 2026; OVapi and ProRail deployment snapshots retrieved 3 September 2026; CC0 for generated NWB/ProRail context
supports: The municipality identifies the N381 as the important Drachten–Oosterwolde–Emmen connection and Hornleger as an industrial/business concentration with about forty organizations and activities through environmental category 4.1. This is land-use context, not live hazardous inventory or plume extent.

Nine monthly NWB border records represent N381, N353, N917, N919, N979, N351 and N380 links to Midden-Drenthe, Heerenveen, Opsterland, Noordenveld and Weststellingwerf. Repeated endpoints of the same corridor are series/shared and their 150 values are logical scenario units, not measured vehicles or emergency capacity.

The scheduled public-transport snapshot has 69 bus stop areas, including Oosterwolde Busstation and Appelscha, while the generated ProRail assignment has no station. Static schedules/geometry do not establish incident operation, accessibility, vehicle capacity, evacuation or external-care continuity.
Residents, recreational visitors, care users, workers and through traffic have different exposure and routing. Resident population cannot be treated as complete daytime or seasonal occupancy.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Electricity-grid planning and current Oosterwolde drinking-water works
evidenceSources.edition: Municipal grid-cooperation and Stationsstraat works pages current in 2026; NBNL snapshot retrieved 2 September 2026; exact NBNL product licence not found
supports: Liander and the municipality describe future 20 kV rings and projects involving Oosterwolde, Appelscha, Donkerbroek, Haule, Haulerwijk and Waskemeer, with the Oosterwolde Noord start planned for 2027. Planning is not present resilience, spare capacity, topology, outage or restoration.

The one NBNL service-area sample, OS OOSTERWOLDE 10-1i, reports 36 MW existing and 37 MW required withdrawal capacity, a 5.5 MW/12-request withdrawal queue, 36 MW existing and 42 MW required injection, a 12 MW/32-request injection queue and seven projects. It is not complete municipal coverage or a live operating state.

Vitens is replacing a transport/main pipe in Stationsstraat, Oosterwolde, in phases in August–November 2026 and 2027, including a boring under the Opsterlandse Compagnonsvaart. A construction plan can change and neither proves an outage nor exposes the full drinking-water topology.
Operator switching, load, pressure, quality, backup power, priority, repair crews, stock and restoration remain Unknown unless a time-valid incident source supplies them.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Rijksdienst voor Digitale Infrastructuur / DUO / RIVM / KNMI / Rijkswaterstaat
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Deployment-cached water, communications, education, care, weather and water-observation coverage
evidenceSources.edition: HWH retrieved 3 September 2026; RDI, DUO, RIVM, KNMI and Waterinfo snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026
supports: GM0085 has 236 partial HWH objects: 204 weirs, fifteen surface-water pumps, six sluices, nine sewer pumps and two wastewater plants. HWH is CC BY-SA 4.0; capacity is null for all weirs, sluices and sewer pumps and five surface pumps. Null is Unknown, not zero capacity.

Both wastewater plants are marked realized, but rwzi Haulerwijk has operating status buiten bedrijf while rwzi Oosterwolde has no such out-of-service flag. The status must be retained exactly; neither record proves live telemetry, process availability, backup or restoration.

The 73 RDI installations comprise 28 mobile, twenty fixed-link, two broadcast, two other-mobile and 21 amateur points; the exact WFS reuse licence is unstated. The 21 DUO education uses comprise thirteen primary, two secondary, one special and five other registrations. Neither dataset establishes coverage, occupancy, emergency role, stock or backup.

There is no municipality-assigned current KNMI weather observation, RIVM PM2.5 point, RIVM SEH, RWS Waterinfo observation or Waterinfo forecast in the deployed point snapshots. Their absence is NoData under bounded point/polygon coverage, not zero weather, smoke, acute-care need, water level, discharge or safety.

evidenceSources.title: E08 — Crisis organization and public municipal emergency contact semantics
evidenceSources.edition: Current public crisis-preparation and municipal emergency-number pages inspected 3 September 2026; no standard reuse licence found
supports: Veiligheidsregio Fryslân describes eight expert teams that support an affected municipality and preparation through plans, training, exercises and cooperation with care and other partners. It does not publish live team availability, deployment, travel time or incident capacity.

The municipal after-hours 14 0516 route includes urgent sewer/pump and public-space problems. It is a reporting/contact channel, not a support point, dispatch guarantee or measured T+72 repair resource.
No reviewed official public source names GM0085 emergency support locations with opening triggers, accessible capacity, overnight space, staff, stock, water, generator endurance or resupply.

First-72-hour actions therefore require explicit owner, authority, proposed/requested/confirmed/completed state, valid time, resources, dependencies, verification and rollback rather than inference from public contact pages.

spatialPlausibility.summary: Eight unrelated hazards reuse one complete neighbourhood order and a controlled local fire does not prioritize its source neighbourhood.

The canonical remote wildfire produces zero direct local fire and 0.250317 smoke at T+24 despite official direct-fire mechanisms in Drents-Friese Wold/Fochteloërveen.

causalTrace.summary: The numerical ledger closes, but local event selection, evidence time, destinations and accountable actions are absent from the causal graph.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to severity, service-stage contributions reconstruct availability and municipal pressure closes numerically.
River selects no local Boven Tjonger/Grootdiep/Kleindiep/Compagnonsvaart boundary or hydrograph; pluvial selects no official footprint, sewer, groundwater, receiving level or control state.

Wildfire selects a remote source rather than local ignition/perimeter/fuel/access; earthquake selects a fixed source rather than a KNMI event/shakemap; cyber and technological incidents select no named target/source or detection.

T+0–6 needs event verification/warning; T+6–24 closures, water/fire control, care routing and support activation; T+24–48 welfare, inspection, repair and resupply; T+48–72 verified restoration, re-entry and unresolved-needs review.

residualLimitations: This deterministic 72-hour planning stress test is not an Ooststellingwerf, Wetterskip Fryslân, Veiligheidsregio Fryslân, KNMI, Liander, Vitens, transport, care or responder forecast, warning, probability, evacuation order, casualty estimate or restoration promise.
No selected local rain field, groundwater state, channel hydrograph, structure/control state, sewer model, official connected footprint, arrival, duration or recession is ingested.

The 0.513332 m river and 0.347866 m pluvial properties are synthetic screening values, not observed or officially modeled local water depths and must not drive evacuation, routing, care or service thresholds.
The generalized boundary and centre do not resolve waterways, controls, terrain, sewers, buildings, roads, nature fuels, facilities, utilities, households or individuals.
CBS values are independently rounded/suppressed; the +15 population difference and null district-heat/charging and other fields are publication semantics, not extra/zero people or assets.
HWH is partial and 236 points do not establish complete topology, compatible capacity, telemetry, live operation, power, backup or restoration; null remains Unknown.
The rwzi Haulerwijk buiten-bedrijf flag is source status and must not be silently normalized; its precise observation/validity and operational implications still require authority confirmation.
Vitens and Liander construction/grid pages are plans with dates, not proof of current failure, completed resilience, live load, pressure, reserve, switching or restoration.
One NBNL sample is planning/queue context, not municipal coverage or operational state.
No complete public causal electricity feeder/switching, drinking-water pipe/pressure/quality, gas district, municipal sewer or telecom backhaul/restoration topology is authorized in the model.
RDI sites do not establish coverage, traffic, ownership, backhaul, power/backup, damage, availability or restoration; exact standard reuse terms were not found.
NWB and GTFS are static geometry/schedule context and do not establish incident road, bus, evacuation, fire, care or logistics continuity; shared corridor sides are non-additive.
Zero in-boundary ProRail stations and RIVM SEH points mean no assigned features in those datasets, not zero travel demand, health care, patients or external acute-care availability.
DUO education locations, the Appelscha visitor centre and ordinary municipal/care sites do not establish command, shelter, distribution or support roles.

No GM0085 Waterinfo observation/forecast, KNMI weather, RIVM PM2.5 or recent seismic-origin point exists in the deployment snapshots; absence is NoData, not normal water, zero weather/smoke/shaking or safety.
Historical Fochteloërveen fire and official Drents-Friese Wold scenarios establish mechanisms, not current ignition, probability, perimeter, occupancy, response time or resources.

The canonical wildfire lacks local ignition/perimeter/fuel/plume/resource evidence; earthquake uses a fixed source; cyber lacks a named target/architecture/detection; compound combines unvalidated assumptions.

Technological risks are publicly identified at class level, but exact current substances, quantities, facility/pipeline state, plume and security-sensitive topology remain Unknown unless explicitly published and authorized.
Recreational visitors, pupils, patients, industrial/agricultural workers and through road/bus users are not represented by resident population or generic service weights.
Household 72-hour preparedness, stocks and ability to assist are not measured; 72 hours is an operations horizon, not guaranteed aid or recovery.

Event-attributable person-hours is a matched-no-event weighted availability proxy, not measured outage-hours, simultaneous deprivation, casualties, displacement or welfare loss; six-hour checkpoints miss fast fire, release, quake, water-control and medical decisions, and 72 hours excludes prolonged recovery.
